chapter: Bands, leaders and radio of the thirties and forties
title: Claude Thornhill's orchestra and Maxine Sullivan's first recording
summary: He recorded in 1937 with Thornhill, including Maxine Sullivan's first record; Hutto notes Thornhill's band and Russ Morgan's were recording-only outfits.

bands.name: Chauncey Morehouse and the Swing Six

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Claude Thornhill had his orchestra and you were a member of that.
Claude Thornhill.
That's right. Do you remember that band?
Yeah.
In 1937 you recorded with him.
It was Maxine Sullivan's first recording.
That's right, that's right.
"Stop, Your Breaking My Heart," was one of the numbers.
Do you remember Claude Thornhill's orchestra or anything about that? Was that the same. I mean did his band or his orchestra sound very much like other dance bands of the time?
Well I would say yes.
Okay.

There is some question on the Swing Six which Chauncey had and Claude Thornhill is on it. And I'm not sure whether...Thornhill at times played vibes, whether Chauncey is playing the vibes or whether Thornhill is playing the vibes.
Oh really.
You think you can hear drums, so that must be Chauncey. So the vibes must be Thornhill.

Right. The discography, Brian Rust at least does list Chauncey as both drums and vibes. That's a good point though. You were only with Claude Thornhill for a very short time. Do you remember why you left him?
Did what?
Do you remember why you left Claude Thornhill?
Claude Thornhill?
Claude Thornhill, you were only with him for a very short time. Do you remember why you left him?
No, I don't remember that.
Okay.
I would think at the time Thornhill was strictly a recording band for his own sessions and backing Maxine Sullivan on Vocalion and on the Victor side.
Yeah.
And he probably didn't have his regular orchestra until about 1941.
Okay but this is the only recording that Chauncey even shows up on.
Right. So the same with the Russ Morgan. Like Chauncey was in Russ Morgan for recording sessions, but probably never was Russ's commercial band.
That's right.
